title: Voice Suture: Mini synthesis of runtime feedback + low-cost patches
content:
Purpose: compact, patch-first synthesis of recent runtime-related customer signals (Apr 2029). Goal is to surface small, testable interventions (<= 2 sprint work) that reduce customer pain and risk while collecting signal for bigger fixes. This is intentionally rough — treat as a sprint-level playbook, not a final roadmap.

Context + sampling:
- Sources: 7 customer calls (CS escalations), support tickets flagged as 'runtime' or 'latency' (month window), two SRE postmortem notes, and a paired field session with Solutions Eng.
- Common thread: customers describe intermittent tail latency spikes, KV-cache warmup behavior causing degraded responses for repeated prompts, and surprising token cost regressions when model fallbacks occur.
- Severity mix: several high-impact reports from enterprise tenants (SLA/throughput impact), many mid-priority from mid-market (developer friction).

Top 6 micro-vignettes (raw):
1) "Chat app: repeated prompt chains after a model update started returning 2–3x slower first-response. Our users noticed lag only after 30–60 minutes of continuous use." — E2E product manager, fintech customer.
2) "We hit a canary where fallback to a quantized variant doubled tokens billed for some prompts — tokenizer/formatting changed subtly and increased whitespace tokens." — infra engineer, commerce customer.
3) "Large batch inference for embeddings had surprising variance across instances; some nodes time out at seq len 2048 despite identical config." — ML infra lead, marketplace.
4) "A private-deploy customer saw KV cache invalidation after our midnight rollout; their chat history lost local cache affinity causing cold-start latencies." — tenant SRE.
5) "Developers want a cheap 'pressure-mode' flag — degrade to shorter generation length and favor deterministic stop tokens when latency SLOs are threatened." — platform PM, early-stage AI startup.
6) "Observability is fine for p95/p99, but we lack a simple per-request flag that ties a customer-visible ticket to an internal trace id for follow-up." — CS ops.

Quick synthesis: patterns and root hints
- KV cache warmup + affinity: several reports point to cache invalidation (rollouts, node churn) rather than core model performance. Warm cache -> good latency; re-warmed -> transient spikes.
- Fallback/variant drift: model variant switching can cause tokenizer/response shape diffs and accidental token-count increases.
- Node-level configuration drift: timeouts/ooms causing variance across nodes suggest rollout/config mismatch or insufficient canary gating.
- Observability gap: CS lacks a low-friction trace id mapping that they can paste into tickets; adds friction to escalations.

Candidate low-cost patches (<= 10 dev-days each) — prioritized by expected customer impact / implementation velocity
A) KV-cache affinity repair linter (owner: eng-infra) — 4 dev-days\- What: a small probe that detects recently-imaged nodes with empty cache and temporarily routes traffic to warmed nodes for the same tenant during rollout windows.\- Why: reduces tail spikes during rollouts without global cache state sharing.\- Risk/notes: routing needs to respect capacity; implement as a conservative heuristic toggle.\- Metrics to watch: p95 latency for affected tenant, cache hit rate, error rate.
B) Token-count regression guard (owner: serving-runtime) — 6 dev-days\- What: add a preflight token diff check in the canary/fallback path: compute token estimate for original and fallback variant; if >15% increase, flag and optionally block fallback.\- Why: prevents silent cost regressions customers observed when fallbacks changed tokenization.\- Risk/notes: estimation must be fast; fallback-blocking should be opt-in for enterprise.\- Metrics: per-request estimated_token_delta, blocked_fallback_count, customer cost delta.
C) Pressure-mode API flag (owner: product-hosted-api + SDK) — 8 dev-days\- What: new API parameter "pressure_mode" with options {latency-first, cost-first, default} that instructs runtime to shorten maximum tokens, tighten sampling temperature, and optionally prefer deterministic stop sequences.\- Why: customers explicitly asked for a lightweight control to trade quality for predictability during load spikes.\- Risk/notes: need SDK and console expose; docs and examples required.\- Metrics: adoption rate, mean generation length, p95 latency under pressure.
D) Trace-id quick-attach (owner: cs-platform) — 3 dev-days\- What: include a human-friendly short trace id in every API response and surface it to CS via logs + ticket attach. Add a one-click copy button in Console request detail.\- Why: lowers friction capturing traces for postmortem and support.\- Risk/notes: verify PII compliance; short id must map into internal trace store.\- Metrics: time-to-triage on support tickets, #tickets with trace id.
E) Canary config validator (owner: release-engineering) — 5 dev-days\- What: CI hook that compares node config + timeout + runtime flags between canary and baseline pools and blocks if mismatch beyond thresholds.\- Why: reduces variance introduced by silent config drift that was causing node-level timeouts.\- Risk/notes: integration with existing release flows required.\- Metrics: canary failures prevented, post-rollout p99 variance.

Lightweight experiments / quick data pulls (<= 2 days) we should run this sprint
- Pull: per-tenant cache-hit time-series for last 60 days; flag correlations with rollouts and image churn (owner: observability).
- Pull: token-count diffs for fallback paths in the last 100k requests across a sample of enterprise tenants (owner: serving-runtime analytics).
- Spike: prototype pressure-mode behavior in sandbox for two willing customers (owner: solutions-eng + eng-hosted-api).

Customer-facing quick-plays (low effort)
- Draft a 1-pager for enterprise customers explaining recommended mitigations during rollouts (cache-affinity policy, suggested console flags). (owner: customer-success)\- Template for 'rollout checklist' that solutions eng can send pre-rollout.

Open questions and decisions needed
- Fallback-blocking UX: should it be default for enterprise, or opt-in? (Decision owners: product + legal)
- Routing heuristic safety: acceptable latency/capacity threshold for holding traffic on warmed nodes? Need SRE input.
- Trace id retention policy: how long to keep mapping for support lookups? Compliance check needed.

Suggested owners & next steps (week-by-week sprint plan)
- Week 0: observability pulls (2d), token-diff pull (2d) — owners: observability, serving-runtime analytics.\- Week 1: start A (kv affinity probe) + D (trace-id UI) in parallel (A: 4d, D: 3d).\- Week 2: start B (token guard) and E (canary validator). Continue A rollout in sandbox.\- Week 3: Docs + pressure-mode API spec + begin SDK stub. Spike with 2 customers.

Communications / stakeholders to loop in now
- Release-eng: for canary validator and rollout heuristics.
- SRE: for routing defaults and capacity safety.
- Legal/Privacy: for trace-id retention and console exposure.
- Solutions Eng: potential pilot customers for pressure-mode spike.

Appendix: useful tickets and links (short)
- JIRA-4821: enterprise latency spike incident (Mar 28 2029)
- JIRA-4899: tokenization delta observed on fallback PR (related to github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1024)
- Confluence KB: runtime-feedback playbook (KB-23)
- Slack thread: customer-voices -> detailed quotes and followups

Notes to self / rough scribbles
- If we can get trace-ids in responses quickly, CS triage time will likely drop by 30–40% (very rough).
- Pressure-mode could be productized later as part of autoscaling + QoS controls for Dedicated tenants.
- Consider exposing a console toggle for 'block token-increasing fallbacks' with an audit log.

Call to action (for reviewers):
- Please add comments inline on priorities and risk appetite.
- Engineering leads: estimate if the dev-day numbers feel off.
- CS / Solutions Eng: volunteer 1–2 pilot customers for pressure-mode spike.

-- end --
